status_summary: HUD published a proposed rule on 2026-03-02 (91 FR 10016) that would let public housing agencies and certain project-based rental assistance owners optionally impose work requirements of up to 40 hours a week for assisted adults aged 18 to 61, with exclusions for disability, primary caregivers, pregnancy, children under 6 and full-time students, and term limits of at least two years in public housing, Housing Choice Vouchers, Project-Based Vouchers and Project-Based Rental Assistance; comments closed on 2026-05-01 and the Federal Register shows no final rule through 2026-10-16. On 2026-09-01 HUD published a revised Operations Notice for the Moving to Work expansion (91 FR 56163) that loosens the safe-harbor limits on optional MTW work requirement and term-limit waivers (40 hours a week per person, no household cap, two-year minimum term), with comments due 2026-11-02 and no effective date confirmed. No statute on the subject was found; the FY2027 budget request, as summarized by a housing advocacy group in April 2026, proposes a mandatory 20-hour weekly work requirement and a five-year assistance cap for HUD rental assistance, which is a request to Congress and not an enacted change.

timeline.event: HUD publishes a proposed rule, Establishing Flexibility for Implementation of Work Requirements and Term Limits (91 FR 10016, amending 24 CFR parts 5, 960, 982 and 983); comments are due 2026-05-01.

HUD publishes a revised Operations Notice for the Moving to Work expansion (91 FR 56163, FR Doc. 2026-17777) that raises the safe-harbor cap for optional MTW work requirements to 40 hours a week per person, deletes the household cap and lowers the minimum term-limit length to two years; comments due 2026-11-02.

uncertainties: The proposed rule and the MTW notice were each read on the Federal Register host for their first 100,000 characters; the unread tails were not checked. The MTW notice states only a comment date, and its text describes two comment periods, so whether the loosened safe harbors already apply to MTW agencies is unconfirmed; if they do, the stage may be understated for those agencies. Absence of a final rule rests on Federal Register API queries through 2026-10-16; White House review status and the Unified Agenda were not checked, and a state-news report of 2026-06-30 that HUD was finalizing the rule is not confirmed by the Federal Register. The FY2027 budget proposal was read in an NLIHC analysis, not the budget document. Executive Order 14394 is a home-construction order (signed 2026-03-13) and is not treated as related. Congressional bills and HUD guidance outside the Federal Register were searched only briefly.
